title: Minestrone
intro: Plenty of summer vegetables simmered slowly until the soup turns thick and sweet.

steps.t: Finely chop the onion, carrots and celery. Dice potatoes and courgettes (1 cm), cut beans, shred cabbage, chop tomatoes.
Soften the chopped onion, carrot and celery in 3 tbsp oil over low heat for 8 minutes, until tender.
steps.label: Base

steps.t: Add the potatoes, green beans, cabbage and tomatoes and stir for 3 minutes, until the cabbage wilts.
steps.label: Veg

steps.t: Pour in the hot stock (store-bought, or salted water, is fine) and bring to the boil.
Lower the heat, half-cover and simmer gently for 40 minutes, stirring now and then.
steps.label: Simmer

pressure.t: Lock the pressure cooker lid and cook for 15 minutes at pressure on low heat, then release.

steps.t: Add the courgettes, peas and borlotti and cook 15 more minutes, until the potatoes break down and it thickens.
steps.label: Finish

pressure.t: Open, add the courgettes, peas and borlotti, and cook uncovered for 10 minutes until thick.

steps.t: Season with salt and pepper, turn off the heat, add the torn basil and let it rest for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Serve hot or warm with a drizzle of raw olive oil.

tips.t: A spoonful of pesto in each bowl makes it minestrone alla genovese (no longer vegan).
For a full meal, cook 150 g ditalini or rice in it for the last 10 minutes (pasta adds gluten).
It's even better the next day; in summer eat it cold, as they do in Liguria.

title: Pasta e fagioli
intro: Partly blended borlotti and ditalini cooked in the soup: creamy without any cream.

steps.t: Finely chop the onion, carrot and celery and soften them in 3 tbsp oil with the garlic and rosemary over low heat.
steps.label: Base

steps.t: Add the passata and chilli and cook for 5 minutes, until it thickens.
steps.label: Tomato

steps.t: Add the beans and hot stock (store-bought is fine) and simmer for 20 minutes.
steps.label: Beans

steps.t: Remove the garlic and rosemary. Blend a third of the beans with some broth and return it to the pot.
Bring back to the boil, add the pasta and cook it in the soup for the time on the pack, stirring often.
steps.label: Pasta

steps.t: If it's too thick, loosen with hot water. Season, turn off the heat and let it rest for 5 minutes.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Serve with a drizzle of raw olive oil and some black pepper.

tips.t: If it needn't be vegan, simmer a Parmesan rind in the broth and lift it out before the pasta.
With dried beans: soak 200 g overnight, then simmer 1½ hours or pressure-cook 25 minutes.

title: Tuscan ribollita
intro: Cavolo nero, beans and stale bread: the farmhouse soup that gets better reheated.

steps.t: Strip the cavolo nero from its stems and shred it with the cabbage. Dice the onion, carrots, celery and potato.
Soften the onion, carrots, celery and garlic in 4 tbsp oil over low heat for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Base

steps.t: Add the crushed tomatoes, potato, cavolo nero and cabbage and stir until the leaves wilt.
steps.label: Greens

steps.t: Mash half the beans and add all of them with the hot stock (store-bought is fine). Cover and simmer 50 minutes.
steps.label: Soup

pressure.t: Mash half the beans, add them all with the stock, lock the pressure cooker and cook 20 minutes at pressure.

steps.t: Thinly slice the bread. In a pot, layer bread and soup, finishing with soup.
Leave to rest for at least 30 minutes, or better overnight in the fridge, until the bread soaks up the broth.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Reheat over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring, until thick enough for a spoon almost to stand up.
steps.label: Reheat

steps.t: Serve with plenty of raw olive oil and black pepper; add thinly sliced red onion if you like.

tips.t: Use unsalted Tuscan bread at least two days old: it holds together and doesn't turn to paste.
It keeps 3 days in the fridge and tastes better every time you reheat it.

title: French onion soup
intro: Long-caramelised onions, beef broth and a cheesy toast melted under the grill.

steps.t: Halve the onions and slice them thinly.
Melt the butter with the oil, add the onions and 1 tsp salt. Cook over medium-low heat for 45 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 2 minutes, until it no longer tastes raw.
steps.label: Flour

steps.t: Deglaze with the wine, scraping the bottom, and boil for 2 minutes until almost evaporated.
steps.label: Wine

steps.t: Pour in the hot stock, add the thyme and bay leaf, and simmer for 20 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Soup

steps.t: Meanwhile toast the baguette slices in the oven at 200 °C for 5 minutes, until dry and golden.
steps.label: Toasts

steps.t: Remove the thyme and bay. Ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls, float two toasts on each and cover with cheese.
Grill at 230 °C for 4–5 minutes, until the cheese bubbles and browns. Careful: the bowls get very hot.
steps.label: Grill

tips.t: Don't turn up the heat to rush the onions: if they stick, add a splash of water and scrape.
Add 2 tbsp cognac with the wine for a deeper flavour.

title: Miso soup
intro: Plant-based kombu and shiitake dashi, silken tofu and miso stirred in at the end.

steps.t: Put the kombu and shiitake in 1 litre of cold water and leave to soak for 30 minutes.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Heat slowly over medium-low heat. Lift out the kombu as soon as small bubbles appear at the edge, before it boils.
steps.label: Dashi

steps.t: Simmer the shiitake for 5 minutes, then lift them out, slice thinly and return them to the broth.
steps.label: Shiitake

steps.t: Meanwhile soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes and drain. Cut the tofu into 1.5 cm cubes.
steps.label: Wakame

steps.t: Add the tofu and wakame to the hot dashi and warm them for 1 minute without boiling.
Turn off the heat. Whisk the miso into a ladle of broth and stir it back in: don't let it boil again.
Serve right away in bowls, topped with sliced spring onion.

tips.t: Boiled miso loses its aroma and turns grainy: always add it off the heat.
For classic dashi (not vegan), add 10 g katsuobushi after the kombu and strain after 2 minutes.

title: Andalusian gazpacho
intro: Chilled soup of ripe tomatoes emulsified with olive oil: refreshing and filling.

steps.t: Chop the tomatoes. Peel the cucumber, keeping a little aside. Seed the pepper. Peel the garlic and remove any green germ.
Soak the bread in cold water for 5 minutes, then squeeze it out well.
steps.label: Bread

steps.t: Blend the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, garlic, bread, salt and vinegar for 2 minutes, until very smooth.
With the blender running, drizzle in the oil until the gazpacho turns pale orange and creamy.
Pass it through a sieve for a silky texture. Thin with cold water if thick, and adjust salt and vinegar.
Chill for at least 2 hours: it should be served ice-cold.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Serve in glasses or bowls with diced cucumber and pepper and a drizzle of oil.

tips.t: With 200 g bread, only tomatoes and no water it becomes salmorejo: top with egg and jamón.
Use very ripe tomatoes, even ugly ones: they bring the sweetness and colour.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge in a closed bottle: shake before serving.

title: Turkish red lentil soup
intro: Silky blended red lentils, finished with chilli-mint oil and plenty of lemon.

steps.t: Rinse the lentils until the water runs clear. Chop the onion and dice the carrot and potato.
Soften the onion in 2 tbsp oil for 5 minutes, then add the carrot, potato, tomato paste and cumin for 2 minutes.
steps.label: Base

steps.t: Add the lentils and hot stock (store-bought is fine). Simmer for 25 minutes, until the lentils fall apart.
steps.label: Lentils

pressure.t: Add the lentils and hot stock, lock the pressure cooker and cook for 8 minutes at pressure. Let it release.

steps.t: Blend with a stick blender until smooth. Thin with hot water if too thick and season with salt.
Heat the remaining oil in a small pan, take it off the heat and add the chilli and mint: it should sizzle, not burn.
Serve the soup with a drizzle of the spiced oil and lemon wedges to squeeze at the table.

tips.t: Serve with warm pita or toasted bread to scoop it up.
It thickens a lot in the fridge: reheat with a little water. Freezes well for 3 months.

title: Tom kha gai
intro: Thai chicken and coconut milk soup, sour with lime and fragrant with lemongrass.

steps.t: Bruise the lemongrass and cut into 4 cm pieces. Slice the galangal, tear the lime leaves, slice mushrooms and chicken.
Bring the stock (store-bought is fine) to the boil with the lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves; simmer 5 minutes.
steps.label: Aromatics

steps.t: Add the coconut milk and chicken and simmer gently for 8 minutes, until cooked through. Don't let it boil hard.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Add the mushrooms and crushed chillies and cook for 3 minutes.
steps.label: Mushrooms

steps.t: Turn off the heat and season with fish sauce, sugar and the lime juice. Taste: sour, salty, a little sweet.
Serve with fresh coriander. Lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves are just for flavour: don't eat them.

tips.t: Serve with a bowl of jasmine rice on the side.
Vegetarian version: tofu for the chicken, veg stock, and soy sauce instead of fish sauce.

title: German potato soup
intro: Potatoes, leek and celeriac, only half blended: thick, rustic and scented with marjoram.

steps.t: Peel and cut the potatoes, carrots and celeriac into 1.5 cm dice. Slice the leek and chop the onion.
Soften the onion and leek in the butter over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, without browning.
steps.label: Leek

steps.t: Add the vegetables, marjoram and hot stock (store-bought is fine). Simmer 20 minutes, until the potatoes are soft.
steps.label: Soup

pressure.t: Add the vegetables, marjoram and stock, lock the pressure cooker and cook for 6 minutes at pressure. Release.

steps.t: Blend about half of the soup with a stick blender, leaving some chunks.
Stir in the cream, nutmeg, salt and pepper and heat for 2 minutes without boiling.
steps.label: Cream

steps.t: Serve piping hot, sprinkled with parsley.

tips.t: German-style: warm sliced frankfurters in the soup or top with crispy bacon (no longer vegetarian).
Serve with buttered rye bread.
